# ------------------------------------------------------ carry-forward fast path
# Evidence follows the DIFF (review.md section 13, EVOLUTION.md 2026-09-04).
# After a fresh-base merge of main the head SHA changes but the PR's own patch
# usually does not; re-dispatching the reviewer for an identical patch cost
# a 15-25 minute round per merge on every other open PR.  When a prior marker
# review exists for a head whose patch hash equals this head's, its verdict and
# ledger are republished for this head (clean or adverse alike, so adjudication
# stays possible) and the reviewer is not dispatched.  --force-review disables.
# patch_hash <base> <head> — sha256 of the diff with the position-dependent
# lines (index, hunk headers) removed: whitespace-SENSITIVE (Lean is
# indentation-sensitive; `git patch-id` would ignore it) but independent of
# where the hunks land after a merge of the base.
patch_hash() {
  git -C "$ROOT" diff --no-color "$1" "$2" | grep -v '^index \|^@@ ' | sha256sum | cut -d' ' -f1
}
carry_forward() {
  local this_pid old old_base old_pid body
  this_pid="$(patch_hash "$(git -C "$ROOT" merge-base "$BASE" "$HEAD_SHA")" "$HEAD_SHA")"
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# review.sh — model-backed review of a GitHub PR, chained after a green CI.
# Account routing passes MIPSTARRE_CODEX_ACCOUNT, MIPSTARRE_ACCOUNT_WAIT and
# MIPSTARRE_CODEX_HOME_SECOND through unchanged to dispatch.sh.
#
# Usage:
#   local/bin/review.sh <pr-number> [--force-review] [--dry-run]
#
#   <pr-number>      GitHub PR number ("12").  Branch, base and head SHA come
#                    from gh_common.py pr-view; the local branch tip must be
#                    exactly the GitHub head before anything is reviewed.
#   --force-review   Review even when the head commit is a bot fix commit.
#                    Used by autofix.sh for the single forced review at the
#                    iteration cap (local/protocols/autofix.md).
#   --dry-run        Resolve the worktree, diff and prompts, print where they
#                    landed, and stop before dispatching an agent.
#
# Local replacement for .github/workflows/pr-review.yml (gate + code-review +
# prose-review jobs).  Protocol: local/protocols/review.md.
#
# GitHub is the record (gh_common.py:4-8).  The gate reads the local-ci/summary
# commit status on the exact head SHA; the verdict is published as ONE COMMENT
# review bound to that SHA plus a local-review/summary status.  Single-account
# repos cannot self-APPROVE, so adverseness travels in the status, never in a
# review state.  There is no local PR record: a GitHub failure fails this
# script closed rather than leaving a fallback record behind.
#
# Exit codes:
#   0  review published, or an intentional skip (kill switch, bot commit, stale
#      head, empty diff)
#   1  usage or environment error
#   3  gate blocked: local-ci/summary is not success for the head SHA.  Nothing
#      is published — the absence of a green local-review/summary is the block.
#   4  the reviewer returned no machine-parseable verdict trailer.  A failing
#      local-review/summary is posted so the PR never reads as green.
#
# Environment:
#   LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED       disables the reviewer on the literal string
#                              "false" only; unset means enabled.
#   MIPSTARRE_TRUSTED_REF      git ref the reviewer personas are read from
#                              (default: main).  Never the branch under review.
#   MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_MODEL     codex model for the code review
#                              (auto: routine Sol, justified hard Astra)
#   MIPSTARRE_PROSE_MODEL      codex model for the blueprint prose review
#                              (default: MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_MODEL)
#   MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT        runtime state root (default ~/.cache/mipstarre-dev)
#   MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_LOCK_WAIT seconds to queue behind another review of the
#                              same PR before giving up (default 1800)
#   MIPSTARRE_DIFF_MAX_LINES   diff lines handed to the reviewer (default 4000)
#   MIPSTARRE_CITATION_MAX_BYTES bytes reserved for the derived blueprint
#                              citation map (default 30000)
#   MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_TIMEOUT   reviewer safety timeout in seconds (default 10800)
#   MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_EFFORT    ultra (required, default)
#   MIPSTARRE_NATIVE_REVIEW_ROOT  root thread servicing native review requests
#   MIPSTARRE_NATIVE_REVIEW_AUTHORS comma-separated author thread IDs (required for native)
#   MIPSTARRE_GITHUB_REPO      owner/repo override for gh_common.py
#
set -euo pipefail

PROG="review.sh"
BIN_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
SELF_ROOT="$(cd "$BIN_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
ROOT="$SELF_ROOT"
# Worktrees are administered from the PRIMARY checkout: when this script runs
# from a linked worktree copy, re-point the git root at the primary (same
# resolution as cache-warmer.sh resolve_primary_repo; EVOLUTION.md 2026-08-30).
# Git operations AND the telemetry ledger copy follow the re-point (telemetry
# is single-instance in the primary, like builds.jsonl); gh_common.py ships
# beside this script and needs no re-point.
_common="$(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir 2>/dev/null || true)"
case "$_common" in
  */.git) ROOT="$(dirname "$_common")" ;;
esac
unset _common
if [ "$ROOT" != "$SELF_ROOT" ] && [ "${MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_REEXEC:-0}" != 1 ] &&
   [ -x "$ROOT/local/bin/review.sh" ]; then
  MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_REEXEC=1 exec "$ROOT/local/bin/review.sh" "$@"
fi

# The one GitHub layer (gh_common.py:6-8); it ships beside this script.
GH_COMMON="$BIN_DIR/gh_common.py"
CACHE="${MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT:-$HOME/.cache/mipstarre-dev}"
TRUSTED_REF="${MIPSTARRE_TRUSTED_REF:-main}"
DISPATCH="$ROOT/local/bin/dispatch.sh"
REVIEW_MODEL="${MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_MODEL:-auto}"
PROSE_MODEL="${MIPSTARRE_PROSE_MODEL:-$REVIEW_MODEL}"
REVIEW_JOB_CLASS="${MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_JOB_CLASS:-independent_review}"
REVIEW_HARDNESS_REASON="${MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_HARDNESS_REASON:-}"
REVIEW_POLICY_ARGS=(--role reviewer --job-class "$REVIEW_JOB_CLASS")
[ -z "$REVIEW_HARDNESS_REASON" ] ||
  REVIEW_POLICY_ARGS+=(--hardness-reason "$REVIEW_HARDNESS_REASON")
REVIEW_MODEL="$(python3 "$BIN_DIR/model_policy.py" "${REVIEW_POLICY_ARGS[@]}" \
  --model "$REVIEW_MODEL" --field model)" || exit 2
PROSE_MODEL="$(python3 "$BIN_DIR/model_policy.py" "${REVIEW_POLICY_ARGS[@]}" \
  --model "$PROSE_MODEL" --field model)" || exit 2
LOCK_WAIT="${MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_LOCK_WAIT:-1800}"
DIFF_MAX_LINES="${MIPSTARRE_DIFF_MAX_LINES:-4000}"
CITATION_MAX_BYTES="${MIPSTARRE_CITATION_MAX_BYTES:-30000}"
REVIEW_TIMEOUT="${MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_TIMEOUT:-10800}"
REVIEW_EFFORT="${MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_EFFORT:-ultra}"
case "$REVIEW_EFFORT" in
  ultra) ;;
  *) echo 'MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_EFFORT must be ultra' >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac
BOT_PREFIX_RE='^\[(claude|codex)-(auto|review)-fix\]'
BLUEPRINT_CITATION_PATH="scripts/blueprint_citations.py"

LOCK_HELD=""

log()  { printf '%s: %s\n' "$PROG" "$*" >&2; }
warn() { printf '%s: warning: %s\n' "$PROG" "$*" >&2; }
die()  { printf '%s: error: %s\n' "$PROG" "$*" >&2; exit 1; }

case "$CITATION_MAX_BYTES" in
  ''|*[!0-9]*) die "MIPSTARRE_CITATION_MAX_BYTES must be an integer of at least 128" ;;
esac
[ "$CITATION_MAX_BYTES" -ge 128 ] ||
  die "MIPSTARRE_CITATION_MAX_BYTES must be an integer of at least 128"

cleanup() {
  local rc=$?; [ -z "${SPARSE_WORKTREE:-}" ] || git -C "$SPARSE_WORKTREE" sparse-checkout disable >/dev/null 2>&1 || warn "could not restore non-sparse checkout at $SPARSE_WORKTREE"
  if [ -n "$LOCK_HELD" ] && [ -d "$LOCK_HELD" ]; then
    rm -rf "$LOCK_HELD"
    LOCK_HELD=""
  fi
  exit "$rc"
}
trap cleanup EXIT INT TERM

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- utilities

now_utc() { date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ; }

# ghc <subcommand> ... — the only way this script talks to GitHub.  gh_common.py
# exits 2 with the reason on stderr and never writes a local fallback record
# (gh_common.py:19-20), so every caller here fails closed.
ghc() { python3 "$GH_COMMON" "$@"; }

# json_get <file> <dotted-path> — one scalar out of a gh_common JSON payload.
# Absent keys print an empty line, so callers test with [ -n ... ] as they did
# with the frontmatter reader this replaces.
json_get() {
  python3 - "$1" "$2" <<'PY'
import json, sys
try:
    data = json.load(open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8"))
except Exception as exc:
    sys.stderr.write("review.sh: unreadable GitHub payload %s: %s\n" % (sys.argv[1], exc))
    raise SystemExit(1)

results/telemetry/owner-audits/reviewer-assessment.json:876: "verdict": "The skeleton is right and should not be rebuilt: gate ordering, head-SHA-bound single COMMENT review with marker idempotency, findings-as-task-list feeding a commit status, trusted-ref personas, double sanitization of the diff as untrusted data, fail-closed on an unparseable verdict, and an auditable adjudication exit. What is not satisfactory is everything about how the model is bounded \u2014 and it is one root cause with four symptoms. The reviewer is given a truncated diff (dispatch.sh caps the attachment at 20,000 bytes regardless of MIPSTARRE_DIFF_MAX_LINES: 2.9% of PR 7's patch, ~19% of PR 5's, and even PR 21's 25.6 KB diff was cut), no memory of prior rounds, no read scope, and no time, turn or byte budget, inside a home directory that contains 130 MB of committed agent transcripts at results/telemetry/sessions/ \u2014 which dispatch.sh keeps growing during the run. So it substitutes filesystem archaeology for diff reading: on PR 21, 326 of 656 commands never named a PR file and produced 83.8% of all tool output; 101 commands mined results/telemetry for 49.7% of the bytes; 20 commands hit the 1 MiB output cap and alone account for 73.2%; the diff was re-derived 277 times with git diff/show/log despite being attached and on disk. The single biggest issue is therefore unbounded scope, not unbounded time \u2014 the missing timeout is what lets it run 106 minutes on 188 changed lines (34 s per changed line, 246x PR 7 round 1), but the missing scope is what makes those minutes worthless. It degrades all four axes at once: precision (findings anchored to whatever it happened to read, PR 21 F10/F11 relitigating settled policy), convergence (memoryless rounds re-raise 8 of 17 on PR 7 round 4; the project's own telemetry diagnosed this on PR 0001 \u2014 \"a fresh reviewer per round has no memory of prior adjudications and unbounded depth\"), cost (34.06M input tokens for 13 findings on a workflow amendment; 217M across 26 runs), and the operator (four PR 7 rounds, 76 model-minutes, zero approvals, terminated only by hand adjudication). The fixes below are all prompt/config/protocol edits totalling roughly 120 lines and add no abstraction layer. One latent item did not earn a slot but is a two-line fix worth doing opportunistically: review.sh executes as $0 from the branch worktree under review, so a PR editing local/bin/review.sh would be reviewed by its own modified reviewer \u2014 have it refuse to run, or re-exec from $ROOT/local/bin/review.sh, after the primary-repo re-point at review.sh:57-68.",

results/telemetry/owner-audits/reviewer-assessment.json:905:     "argument": "The proposal is refuted on its own factual premise and on three independent safety grounds. Evidence is from ~/MIPStarRE-qpbt and ~/.cache/mipstarre-dev on ghz.\n\n1) THE PREMISE IS FALSE. \"PR 21 ... with nothing that will ever stop it\" \u2014 it stopped. results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl records `reviewer-pr21-20260902-01 wall_s=6598 status=done`; the dispatch log ends with a `turn.completed` event carrying usage {input_tokens: 34,056,619, output_tokens: 152,179}; ~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/reviews/pr21/7f5c58ba.../code.rc = 0. The run published a real review: 13 findings, two blockers, `VERDICT: CHANGES_REQUESTED` (pr21/ledgers/pr21-7f5c58ba...md) \u2014 on a PR whose entire purpose is retiring a merge-time safety gate. F1 is a genuine TOCTOU in autofix.sh cap accounting (`:402-408` computed before the lock at `:541-543`); F2 is that `pr_merge.py --adjudicated` accepts a body that merely starts with ADJUDICATION and contains `head=<sha>`. With `timeout 2400`, that review dies at minute 40 (~36% through), review.sh posts local-review/summary=failure, and the record's most safety-relevant ledger is never written. The proposal's own expected_effect (\"a run that would have burned 34M tokens self-terminates with a usable ledger instead of being killed empty\") inverts what actually happens: the unchanged lane self-terminated with a usable ledger; the proposal is what kills it empty.\n\n2) THE DEFAULT DESTROYS 15% OF ALL SUCCESSFUL REVIEWS EVER RUN. From sessions.jsonl, of 26 reviewer sessions with status=done, four exceed 2400 s: reviewer-pr0001-...-07 = 2657, reviewer-pr5-...-01 = 3622, reviewer-pr5-...-02 = 3609, reviewer-pr21-...-01 = 6598. PR 5 is the ONLY PR in the record that ever converged \u2014 findings 5, 4, 4, 0, ending `VERDICT: APPROVED` (pr5/b5da371.../code-last-message.md). Its rounds 1 and 2 \u2014 the two rounds that found the 5 and 4 real defects that drove the convergence \u2014 both exceed the proposed cap by ~20 minutes and would have been killed with zero output. A bound whose default deletes both productive rounds of the only converging review is not a safety net; it is a defect filter tuned to remove the expensive findings.\n\n3) IT DEADLOCKS THE MERGE GATE AND MAKES \u00a712 ADJUDICATION UNREACHABLE. pr_merge.py check_review raises `GateFailure(\"gate 4 (review): no review carrying <marker> on commit ...\")` BEFORE it ever consults the `adjudicated` flag or looks for an ADJUDICATION comment. A timeout publishes no marker-bound review at all. So a PR whose honest review exceeds the cap can be merged neither by verdict nor by operator adjudication \u2014 review.md \u00a712's only escape hatch requires a published review on that exact head. Re-running is deterministic: same diff, same corpus, same wall. The proposal converts \"slow but eventually correct\" into \"permanently unmergeable until the operator discovers and raises an undocumented env var,\" which is a worse failure mode than the stall it targets, and it silently rewrites the \u00a712 contract.\n\n4) THE BUDGET SENTENCE OPENS A FAIL-OPEN APPROVE. review.sh's parser injects a synthetic blocking finding only when the ledger is empty AND the verdict is not APPROVED (`if not entries and verdict != \"APPROVED\"`). An APPROVED trailer over `- none` yields UNRESOLVED_TOTAL=0, and review.sh:1043-1047 then sets SUMMARY_STATE=success, which gate 4 reads as clean. \"When either is spent, emit the Findings ledger and VERDICT from what you already have\" explicitly authorizes a verdict on incomplete evidence, and on a diff where nothing has surfaced in the first 120 commands the compliant output is APPROVED with an empty ledger. Nothing downstream \u2014 not the ledger, not the status, not the marker \u2014 records that the review was truncated. Today a stalled reviewer posts no status and nothing merges (fail-safe); after this change a budget-truncated reviewer can post a green status (fail-open). That is a direct precision-and-safety regression.\n\n5) THE 120-COMMAND FIGURE IS MEASURABLY BELOW WHERE THE FINDINGS COME FROM. Indexing PR 21's dispatch log by command_execution order: the first command touching .github/prompts/auto-fix-* is #119, docs/pr_review_management.md #127, gh_common.py #144, docs/CONTRIBUTING.md #171. Findings F12, F10, F9 are built on exactly those reads, and F10 is the finding that the PR's replacement of user consent with operator adjudication contradicts the pinned \"never merge without consulting the user\" rule. A 120-command budget deletes three findings including the governance one. Worse, F5 (\"the amendment cites a PR #5 telemetry incident absent from this head\") is only derivable by grepping results/telemetry \u2014 the corpus the companion measurement lane calls pure waste. Off-diff reading is not this reviewer's overhead; it is where its cross-file contract findings come from. Cutting it by clock or command count cuts precision, not fat.\n\n6) THE COST CLAIM IS BACKWARDS. Tokens bill as the turn proceeds; killing at 2400 s does not refund them. PR 5 round 1 would have burned roughly 12M of its 18.5M input tokens for zero output and then needed a full re-run \u2014 run_agent never passes --resume, so nothing is recoverable. The change can raise total spend on precisely the PRs it claims to protect. The measured lever that actually saves money without losing findings is scope, not clock: 101 of PR 21's 658 commands named results/telemetry and returned 49.7% of all tool output. An `.rgignore` for results/telemetry/sessions/ plus moving dispatch.sh's tee target out of the worktree removes ~half the cost while keeping every finding \u2014 cheaper in lines than this proposal and strictly dominant on the same objective.\n\n7) TWO MECHANICAL DEFECTS. (a) `timeout N codex ... | tee \"$CAPTURE\"` (dispatch.sh:631) bounds codex, not the pipeline: PIPESTATUS[0] is only evaluated after tee sees EOF, and codex's sandboxed `/bin/bash -lc` children inherit the stdout pipe, so a child outliving SIGTERM leaves the \"hard wall clock\" soft. It needs `timeout -k 30` at minimum. (b) The ~8 lines proposed for run_agent are dead code: review.sh:941-945 already posts `post_summary failure` and dies whenever the lane exits non-zero with an empty CODE_OUT, and a timeout-killed codex writes no `-o` file, so rc=124 already flows through that path. The proposal's own line budget is therefore mostly the kill and the prose.\n\n8) THE STATED HARM IS OVERSTATED. LOCK_DIR is `$CACHE/locks/review-$PR_NUM.lock` (review.sh:438) \u2014 per-PR. A runaway on PR 21 blocks only another review of PR 21, never the queue at large, so \"holding the per-PR lock while any queued review times out\" does not generalize.\n\nWhat survives: a runaway guard is worth having, but as a guard against a genuinely hung process, not as a latency control, and it must never be able to produce a green or a silent gap.",
results/telemetry/owner-audits/reviewer-assessment.json:906:     "amendment": "Do the scope fix first, then add a guard that cannot fail open or fail stuck.\n\n(a) Ship the scope fix alone and re-measure before capping anything: add `results/telemetry/sessions/` to a `.rgignore` in the review worktree and move dispatch.sh's event-stream tee target out of the repo into $CACHE, so the reviewer stops grepping 130 MB of prior agent transcripts (49.7% of PR 21's tool output). Re-derive the wall-clock distribution from sessions.jsonl after two or three reviews; any cap chosen before this is fitted to a cost driver that is about to disappear.\n\n(b) If a guard is still wanted, set it from the observed distribution, not intuition: `timeout -k 30 ${MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_TIMEOUT:-9000}` (2.5 h). Observed completed runs are 2657 / 3609 / 3622 / 6598 s; 2400 s sits below the 85th percentile and kills 15% of successful history. 9000 s kills nothing in the record while still bounding a truly hung process. Verify the pipeline actually dies (children inherit the tee pipe) rather than assuming rc=124 arrives.\n\n(c) Make expiry reachable by the protocol. On rc=124, publish a marker-bound review on the exact head whose body is `## Findings` / `- [ ] F1 (blocker) - \u2014 reviewer exceeded the wall-clock guard at Ns; no verdict was reached` and `VERDICT: CHANGES_REQUESTED`, alongside local-review/summary=failure. That keeps the exact-head/marker invariant intact, keeps the PR blocked, and \u2014 unlike a bare status \u2014 leaves gate 4's `if not matching` satisfied so review.md \u00a712 operator adjudication remains available. Without this, a capped PR is unmergeable by every path the protocol defines.\n\n(d) If the budget sentence is kept, it must forbid a green outcome. Replace \"emit the Findings ledger and VERDICT from what you already have\" with: \"If you exhaust your budget before finishing, emit the ledger you have, add `- [ ] F0 (blocker) - \u2014 review incomplete: budget exhausted after N commands; areas not covered: ...`, and emit `VERDICT: CHANGES_REQUESTED`. Never emit APPROVED or COMMENTED from an unfinished review.\" Add a matching assertion in write_review so an APPROVED trailer that carries the incompleteness marker is rejected the same way a missing trailer is. Without this clause the sentence is a licence for a truncated APPROVE that review.sh:1043-1047 turns into a success status and pr_merge.py reads as clean.\n\n(e) Do not add a command-count budget at 120. PR 21's first reads of docs/pr_review_management.md, gh_common.py and docs/CONTRIBUTING.md are commands #127, #144 and #171, and findings F9, F10, F12 depend on them. If a count is ever added, calibrate it above the observed index at which cross-file contract findings are formed (>=300 on this evidence), and treat it as a prompt for the reviewer to start converging, not as a stop.\n\n(f) Drop the \"~8 lines in run_agent\" item: review.sh:941-945 already handles a non-zero lane exit with empty output. The real net change is (b)+(c)+(d)."
results/telemetry/owner-audits/reviewer-assessment.json:912:     "argument": "The diagnosis is right (there is no wall anywhere in the review path) but the prescription, at its stated default and with its stated failure handling, makes reviews worse on this repo's own recorded corpus. Six attacks, all with evidence.\n\n1. THE DEFAULT KILLS THE THREE MOST PRODUCTIVE RUNS IN THE CORPUS. results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl holds 28 reviewer sessions with wall_s = [1,365,685,895,969,1134,1160,1200,1225,1325,1382,1393,1425,1430,1445,1505,1527,1555,1760,1892,1895,2036,2106,2180,2657,3609,3622,6598]. A 2400 s wall is p86: it kills 4/28 (14.3%); 2700 kills 3/28. Every one of those four finished with status \"done\". Two of them are PR 5 rounds 1 and 2 (reviewer-pr5-20260902-01, 3622 s; -02, 3609 s), which produced the 5-finding and 4-finding ledgers (~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/reviews/pr5/3b394f23.../code-last-message.md and f36df43c...) that carried PR 5 down 5 -> 4 -> 4 -> 0 to the only APPROVED verdict in the whole dataset (b5da371d..., \"VERDICT: APPROVED\", 0 unchecked). Under the proposal both are SIGTERMed at 40 min, publish nothing, and post local-review/summary=failure. The change's first effect on real history is to delete the evidence that produced the project's only convergence.\n\n2. PR 21 IS NOT A RUNAWAY \u2014 IT FINISHED, AND THE PROPOSAL WOULD HAVE MADE IT UNMERGEABLE FOREVER. reviewer-pr21-20260902-01 recorded wall_s=6598, status done; code-last-message.md is 8695 B with 13 unchecked findings and \"VERDICT: CHANGES_REQUESTED\". Now the trap: pr_merge.py check_review (local/bin/pr_merge.py:161-168) raises `if not matching` \u2014 no review carrying the marker on the head \u2014 BEFORE it ever reaches the `if not adjudicated` branch at :184. A head that never receives a published review fails gate 4 with AND without --adjudicated, and review.md section 12 requires the ADJUDICATION comment to list \"the last round's findings\", which do not exist. PR 21's length is structural (unscoped search surface), not variance, so every retry is killed at the same wall. The proposal converts \"slow review, real verdict, red status the author can act on\" into \"no verdict, no sanctioned merge path, ever\". That is strictly worse than the status quo, in which a slow review still lands a verdict.\n\n3. THE BUDGET SENTENCE MANUFACTURES A GREEN MERGE OUT OF PARTIAL EVIDENCE. code-task.md's required output format admits exactly three trailers \u2014 APPROVED, COMMENTED, CHANGES_REQUESTED \u2014 and \"- none\" is a legal ledger. review.sh: \"Clean = APPROVED, or COMMENTED with zero unchecked findings\" -> local-review/summary=success; pr_merge.py:179 then passes gate 4. Nothing downstream can distinguish \"reviewed fully, clean\" from \"budget spent at command 120, nothing found yet\". Telling the model \"when either is spent, emit the Findings ledger and VERDICT from what you already have\" therefore creates a path where an unfinished review merges the PR. This is precisely what the round-cap design deliberately routes through a human: today merging on incomplete evidence requires the operator to sign an ADJUDICATION comment naming the exact head; the budget sentence lets the model do it silently. \"A partial review is useful\" is false here \u2014 a partial review is a green light.\n\n4. THE EVIDENCE IS BACK-LOADED, SO TRUNCATION COSTS PRECISION AND ADDS CHURN. PR 21's dispatch log has 658 commands. A 2400 s cut falls at command ~174 (byte-proportional) or ~239 (call-rate uniform, 10.1 s/call) \u2014 64-74% of the run is after the wall. Everything the final ledger cites as validation is after it: `bash -n .githooks/pre-commit local/bin/autofix.sh` (idx 324), the workflow suite (326), full discovery (488, 494). Worse, commands 570-654 are the reviewer proving that the one red test, scripts/tests/test_generate_badges.py:309, is pre-existing and environmental \u2014 `git diff --quiet a7e5a38..HEAD -- scripts/tests/test_generate_badges.py`, `git blame -L 300,315`, a /dev/shm reproduction \u2014 which is why the published review says \"reproduced one unrelated existing failure ... because that test writes to /tmp in this read-only environment\". Under a 30-minute self-budget the reviewer reaches discovery, sees red, and has no budget left to exculpate. The likely output is a blocker finding against a file the PR does not touch. The proposal changes the prompt spec (~10 lines) and budgets zero lines for the writer, so a `- [x] F7 (advisory)` from the model still lands as `- [ ] F7 (advisory)` in the published body and still blocks. Worse, the model is now told advisories are free, so it will write more of them \u2014 every one arriving as a blocker. Net effect: a larger blocking ledger, not a smaller one.\nThis is not speculative: PR 7 round 4 F10 is literally `- [ ] F10 (changes) local/bin/review.sh:728 \u2014 Canonicalization turns advisory-only feedback into a merge blocker`. The reviewer already found this bug, at that exact line, and it is still open. The proposal restates the symptom and patches the wrong layer.\n\n**2. The premises are factually wrong.** \"advisory_findings_ever_published: 0\" and \"the prompt forbids labelling anything non-blocking\" are both false.\n- PR 21's published ledger (`~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/reviews/pr21/7f5c58ba\u2026-combined.md`) is **2 blocker + 10 changes + 1 advisory** \u2014 F13 `scripts/tests/test_github_workflow.py:413` carries `(advisory)`. So the reviewer does use the label, and it applied it to 1 of 13 findings. The claimed \"13-finding advisory-grade review reads as a wall\" is contradicted by the reviewer's own severities: 12 of 13 are \ud83d\udd34/\ud83d\udfe1. There is no blanket ban; earlier ledgers had no advisories because the reviewer judged those items \ud83d\udfe1/\ud83d\udd34, which line 8 says \"must be addressed before approval\" and line 50 repeats. Routing \ud83d\udfe1 findings out of the gate via the local contract (authoritative per review.md \u00a73) silently overrides a substantive review criterion that review.md's own header claims is unchanged by the port.\n\n**3. \"From round 3, only blocker-severity net-new findings may be added\" would have merged known-bad code \u2014 demonstrably, on the only PR that ever converged.**\nPR 5 ran 5 \u2192 4 \u2192 4 \u2192 0 findings and ended `VERDICT: APPROVED` at round 4. Round 3 (`99ccb0c1\u2026-combined.md`) carried four findings, **all severity `changes`**: a `polyFunc` abbreviation duplicating the existing LDT declaration \"contrary to the binding brief\", an empty second public name, transitively redundant imports, duplicate question-support definitions. Under the proposal all four are barred from the ledger, unresolved drops to 0, verdict falls to COMMENTED, `local-review/summary=success`, gate 4 passes, and PR 5 is mergeable at round 3 with all four defects in. The actual loop blocked, the author fixed them, and round 4 returned a clean APPROVED. The proposal removes the exact mechanism that produced this project's only approval \u2014 and PR 5 also refutes \"review.sh will produce full-size ledgers forever / nothing pushes the finding count down.\"\nPR 7 round 4 is the same shape: 10 of its 17 findings are `changes`, including F11-F14 against `pr_open.py`/`agent.sh` \u2014 files round 3 never flagged, i.e. net-new defects in the fix commits. Under the proposal those ten leave the gate and go to prose, where, by the contract's own words, \"an issue you do not write here is not tracked anywhere else.\" \u00a712 exists so that \"nothing is dropped silently: an adjudicated finding lives on as an issue.\" The proposal drops them silently instead \u2014 it defeats \u00a712's stated property rather than mechanizing it.\n\n**4. Severity becomes load-bearing on the merge gate, and severity is a model judgement over attacker-controlled input.**\nToday mislabelling severity is harmless: `SUMMARY_STATE=success` iff verdict \u2208 {APPROVED, COMMENTED} **and** `UNRESOLVED_TOTAL=0`, and every finding counts. Make advisories non-blocking and the gate becomes \"whatever the model typed in the parentheses.\" Note the fallback at review.sh:714: an unrecognised severity containing `advis` **or `nit`** is coerced to advisory. The diff is the one input an attacker controls (review.md \u00a74, DESIGN invariant 6); an injected nudge \u2014 or plain drift \u2014 that gets one finding written as `(nit)` now un-blocks it. This converts a robust structural gate into a model-judgement gate, in the direction of permitting merges.\n\n**5. The round counter over-counts, so the escalation fires on PRs that never had those rounds.**\n`post_review` (gh_common.py:242-262) is idempotent per `(commit_id, marker)`, so counting marker-bound reviews counts **distinct reviewed heads over the PR's whole life**, not review-fix iterations. Worse, `autofix.sh:599-603` calls `review.sh \"$PR_NUM\" --force-review` for the terminal review at the fix cap (`MIPSTARRE_FIX_CAP` default 5) \u2014 bot-fix heads that rung 7 normally skips get reviews anyway. Change the writer to route `sev == \"advisory\"` entries out of the checkbox ledger into a separate `## Advisory (non-blocking)` section rendered as plain bullets \u2014 `* (advisory) path:line \u2014 summary` \u2014 which `^\\s*[-*]\\s*\\[ \\]` cannot match in either `combine_review` or `pr_merge.py:174`. That closes PR7-R4-F10, shrinks the wall, and never lets the model's severity string decide mergeability by way of the `advis|nit` coercion at review.sh:714. Pair it with a \u00a79 amendment stating that advisory findings are not tracked by the gate and that anything worth tracking must be a blocker/changes finding or a filed issue \u2014 otherwise the contract's \"an issue you do not write here is not tracked anywhere else\" becomes false. Leave the trusted prompt untouched: it already says \ud83d\udfe1/\ud83d\udd34 must be fixed, and review.md's header promises the substantive criteria are unchanged.\n\n**Keep the round counter and the banner, but make both informational and safe.**\n- Derive the count from review-fix iterations, not from `pulls/N/reviews` rows: exclude reviews whose head subject matched the rung-7 bot-fix pattern (the `autofix.sh:603 --force-review` terminal reviews) and whose commit is not an ancestor of the current head, so rebases and amends do not consume rounds. Interpolate it as pure context \u2014 \"this is review #N on this PR; \u00a712 caps the loop at four\" \u2014 and gate no reviewer behaviour on it.\n- Build the \u00a712 banner **inside `combine_review`, before** the `UNCHECKED` count and before the `$TELEMETRY_DIR` copy, and add a one-line guard that refuses to publish if the banner text matches `^\\s*[-*]\\s*\\[ \\]`, so the status and gate 4 can never disagree and the banner can never become a permanent block.\n\n**Spend the remaining budget where the evidence points.** The measured pathology is cost and scope, not ledger size: wrap the `codex exec` call in `timeout ${MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_TIMEOUT:-2700}` and treat a timeout as an empty-output failure (`post_summary failure`); add an explicit read-scope exclusion for `results/telemetry/` and `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/` to the local execution contract (or move the dispatch tee target out of the worktree); and pass the previous round's ledger as a second `--context-file` so \"previous feedback\" is supplied rather than hunted. live root, complete author

policy against the current invocation, then reuses the ordinary rollout
validation and telemetry record. The unchanged parser, lane writer, combiner and
idempotent `gh_common.py` publisher consume the resulting final messages. A resume
uses a fresh scratch directory and retains the original prompt paths inside the
rebuilt task text, leaving canonical prompts and old outputs unchanged. It does
not change the reviewed worktree's sparse-checkout state. A failed acceptance in
either lane, or an unparseable completed verdict in a combined resume, publishes no review or
summary. Queued, dry-run, stale, mismatched, already-published, or concurrently
published continuations fail closed. Reviewer reuse and source mutation remain
held until the canonical publisher consumes the responses; local acceptance of
one lane alone does not release either hold.

Routine reviews default to Sol through `MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_JOB_CLASS=independent_review`.
For a genuinely hard/semantic/control-policy review main sets `hard_review` and
`MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_HARDNESS_REASON`; it selects Astra and records that reason in
the native request. Explicit conflicting model overrides fail. The model choice
does not change identity independence, author exclusion, CI or any merge gate.
Existing Astra reviewers need a fresh explicit Sol spawn for future routine jobs,
not a follow-up treated as a model switch. This control-policy PR itself requires Astra.

Missing pieces degrade with a message, never silently: missing CI statuses
block, no `worktree-setup.sh` warns about a cold build cache, no codex CLI is a
hard error.  A GitHub failure is fatal — a verdict that cannot be published is
not a verdict.

# fetch_trusted <repo-relative-path> <dest> — reviewer prompts come from the
# committed default branch, never from the branch under review (DESIGN.md
# invariant 5; pr-review.yml:140-146, the .trusted-actions checkout).
fetch_trusted() {
  if ! git -C "$ROOT" show "$TRUSTED_REF:$1" >"$2" 2>/dev/null; then
    die "cannot read trusted prompt '$1' from ref '$TRUSTED_REF'. The reviewer persona must come from committed $TRUSTED_REF (DESIGN.md invariant 5); commit .github/prompts/ there or set MIPSTARRE_TRUSTED_REF."
  fi
}

# resolve_worktree <branch> — same resolution order as ci.sh: git's own
# registry first, then the .worktrees/<branch> convention.  Creates it if the
# branch has no worktree yet.
resolve_worktree() {
  local branch="$1" found="" safe dest have
  found="$(git -C "$ROOT" worktree list --porcelain 2>/dev/null |
    awk -v b="refs/heads/$branch" '
      /^worktree /{p=substr($0,10)}
      $0 == "branch " b {print p; exit}')"
  if [ -n "$found" ] && [ -d "$found" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$found"
    return 0
  fi
  safe="$(printf '%s' "$branch" | tr '/' '-')"
  dest="$ROOT/.worktrees/$safe"
  if [ -e "$dest" ]; then
    have="$(git -C "$dest" rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD 2>/dev/null || true)"
    if [ "$have" = "$branch" ]; then
      printf '%s\n' "$dest"
      return 0
    fi
    die "$dest exists but is not a worktree of '$branch' (HEAD: ${have:-not a git worktree}); run 'git -C $ROOT worktree prune' or remove it"
  fi
  mkdir -p "$ROOT/.worktrees"
  git -C "$ROOT" worktree add --quiet "$dest" "$branch" ||
    die "git worktree add $dest $branch failed"
  if [ -x "$ROOT/local/bin/worktree-setup.sh" ]; then
    "$ROOT/local/bin/worktree-setup.sh" "$dest" >&2 ||
      warn "worktree-setup.sh failed for $dest; the reviewer runs without a warmed build cache"
  else
    warn "local/bin/worktree-setup.sh not found; the reviewer worktree has no warmed Lean build cache (local/protocols/build-cache.md)"
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$dest"
}

# run_agent <role> <sandbox> <worktree> <persona-path> <task-file>
#           <standalone-prompt> <context-file> <out-file> <model>
#
# All codex invocations go through local/bin/dispatch.sh when it exists, so the
# session lands in results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl (DESIGN.md, "Agent
# sessions").  The fallback is a direct codex exec with a loud warning.
run_agent() {
  local role="$1" sandbox="$2" wt="$3" persona="$4" taskfile="$5"
  local standalone="$6" ctx="$7" out="$8" model="$9"
  local dlog="$out.dispatch.log" task_text last rc=0
  model="$(python3 "$BIN_DIR/model_policy.py" "${REVIEW_POLICY_ARGS[@]}" \
    --model "$model" --effort "$REVIEW_EFFORT" --field model)" || return 4
  task_text="$(cat "$taskfile")"

  if [ -n "${MIPSTARRE_NATIVE_REVIEW_ROOT:-}" ]; then
    local native_args=(--job-class "$REVIEW_JOB_CLASS" --model "$model")
    [ -z "$REVIEW_HARDNESS_REASON" ] ||

This archive preserves the exact evidence for deploying the paired CODE/PROSE
native-review continuation in PR #476 and using it once on the two completed
PR #400 responses whose original publisher had terminated.

`4c343e6c88b7714a3bbf121b3dc23839df303e3e`, with all nine contexts green,
then received independent hard review approval `5147206622`. The service gate
merged it as `81148545f0752ec09b3efe88332b49bb771312be`. A later attempted CI
launch was refused by the existing canonical lock before it started jobs or
wrote statuses; it was not a second CI run.

The service boundary parked five build rows and four session rows while holding
only the actual JSONL inode locks. It released both locks before service, then
restored the parked rows ahead of later appends with the same inodes, exact
prefixes, order, multiplicity, and valid JSON. No global writer-idle wait or
clean-tree gate relaxation was used.

After the merge, the archived command consumed the preserved PR #400 CODE and
PROSE responses through the deployed trust, parser, combiner, head, CI, lock,
and publication guards. Canonical review `5147250926` recorded two CODE and
five PROSE findings. No review was restarted, no response was edited, and the
source worktree remained unchanged. PR #400 is therefore not merge eligible.

and its byte-preserving compressed patch are evidence for the next normal
checked-publication, CI, and fresh-review cycle; they are not recorded as
